group.title: In the classroom
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A big white board on the wall that the teacher writes on.
examples: The teacher writes on the {whiteboard}.
wrong: We sleep on the whiteboard at night.

words.meaning: A small thing that takes away pencil marks.
examples: Can I use your {eraser}?
wrong: I use my eraser to make my words darker.

words.meaning: A flat stick for drawing straight lines.
examples: Draw a line with your {ruler}.
wrong: I use my ruler to draw round circles.

words.meaning: A tool with two blades for cutting paper.
examples: Cut the paper with {scissors}.
wrong: I drink water from my scissors.

words.meaning: A sticky thing that holds paper together.
examples: Put {glue} on the back of the picture.
wrong: I use glue to take the pictures off the paper.

words.meaning: A pencil that draws in a color, like red or green.
examples: Draw the grass with a green {colored pencil}.
wrong: My colored pencil only writes in no color at all.

words.meaning: A thick pen with bright ink.
examples: Write your name with a red {marker}.
wrong: My marker writes nothing because it is full of ink.

words.meaning: A bag for carrying your books to school.
examples: My books are in my {schoolbag}.
wrong: I wear my schoolbag on my feet.

words.meaning: A small bag or box for your pens and pencils.
examples: My pens are in my {pencil case}.
wrong: I keep my lunch soup in my pencil case.

words.meaning: A small tool that makes the end of a pencil sharp.
examples: My pencil is not sharp. Where is the {pencil sharpener}?
wrong: I use my pencil sharpener to make my pencil longer.

words.meaning: What you say or write after a question.
examples: Write your {answer} in the box.
wrong: The answer came before anybody asked a question.

words.meaning: All the letters from A to Z.
examples: Children learn the {alphabet} in their first year.
wrong: The alphabet has only three letters.

words.meaning: The number on a page of a book.
examples: Look at {page number} ten.
wrong: The page number tells you the name of the writer.

words.meaning: What a word tells you.
examples: What is the {meaning} of this word?
wrong: The meaning of ’hot’ is ’cold’.

words.meaning: The rules for putting words together in a language.
examples: We study English {grammar} on Tuesdays.
wrong: Grammar is the color of the classroom walls.

words.meaning: The language of the US, the UK and many other countries.
examples: We speak {English} in this class.
wrong: English is a fruit that grows on trees.

words.meaning: To put your arm up to ask or answer.
examples: {Raise your hand} if you know the answer.
wrong: Raise your hand by putting it in your pocket.

words.meaning: To draw a ring around something.
examples: {Circle} the right answer.
wrong: Circle the word by drawing a straight line under it.

words.meaning: To draw a line under a word.
examples: {Underline} the verbs in the text.
wrong: Underline the word by drawing a line above it.

words.meaning: A child who goes to school.
examples: There are twenty {pupils} in my class.
wrong: The pupil teaches all the teachers at the school.

words.meaning: A kind of exercise where you say if a sentence is right or wrong.
examples: Read the sentences and write {true or false}.
wrong: In true or false you draw a picture of a cat.

words.meaning: A few people together.
examples: We work in a {group} of four.
wrong: A group is one person alone.

words.meaning: A short time to rest between lessons.
examples: We play outside at {break}.
wrong: During the break we work very hard on a test.

words.meaning: A thing that rings to tell you a time.
examples: The {bell} rings at three, and school is over.
wrong: The bell is so quiet that nobody can hear it ring.

words.meaning: A white stick for writing on a dark board.
examples: The teacher writes with {chalk}.
wrong: I write on the board with chalk made of ice cream.

words.meaning: A big picture or notice on a wall.
examples: There is a {poster} of animals on the wall.
wrong: The poster is so small you cannot see it.

words.meaning: A paper with exercises for students to do.
examples: Do the {worksheet} in pencil.
wrong: I read the worksheet on the radio.

words.meaning: A small metal cupboard at school where you keep your things.
examples: I put my coat in my {locker}.
wrong: I keep my horse in my school locker.

words.meaning: Special clothes that all students at a school wear.
examples: Our school {uniform} is blue and white.
wrong: Every student wears a different uniform in every color.

words.meaning: A big letter, like A, B or C.
examples: Start your name with a {capital letter}.
wrong: A capital letter is the smallest letter.

words.meaning: The sign ? at the end of a question.
examples: Put a {question mark} after ’Who are you’.
wrong: Put a question mark at the end of ’I am happy.’

words.meaning: The way the letters of a word are written.
examples: Check your {spelling} before you hand it in.
wrong: My spelling is the way I say a word.

words.meaning: To put colors on a picture with pens or crayons.
examples: {Color} the apple red.
wrong: Color the picture with only water and no paint.

words.meaning: A pen with bright ink to mark important words.
examples: Mark the new words with a yellow {highlighter}.
wrong: I use my highlighter to make the words disappear.

words.meaning: Words you say when something is not clear to you.
examples: Sorry, {I don’t understand}. Can you say it again?
wrong: I don’t understand, he said, and then he explained it all.

words.meaning: A small card with a word or picture to help you learn.
examples: The teacher shows a {flashcard} with a cat.
wrong: A flashcard is a big table for the class.

words.meaning: A tool that joins papers with small metal pins.
examples: Use the {stapler} to join the pages.
wrong: I use a stapler to cut paper in half.

words.meaning: A small bent wire that holds papers together.
examples: Hold the pages with a {paper clip}.
wrong: I use a paper clip to write my name.

words.meaning: To hear words and then say them again.
examples: {Listen and repeat} after me: ’apple’.
wrong: Listen and repeat means say nothing at all.

words.meaning: A small box for carrying your lunch to school.
examples: My sandwich is in my {lunchbox}.
wrong: I keep my pencils and books in my lunchbox and my lunch in my pencil case.
